note: 40 useful cards carried forward from PRs #58, #59, #61, #62 and #66. Not active yet; promote at most ten in a later combined batch after duplicate screening.

card.t: P1-05 · Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana · Crowding-out effect
card.hook: Crowding out = Government borrowing ↑ → competition for savings → interest rates may ↑ → private investment may ↓.
card.scene: Imagine the government and private firms seeking loans from the same pool of savings. If the pool does not grow, one borrower can make funds costlier for the other.
card.trap: Crowding out is a possible mechanism, not an automatic result in every economy. Spare capacity and productive public investment can change the outcome.
card.q: In the standard crowding-out channel, what can happen to private investment when deficit-financed government borrowing rises?
card.a: It may fall if borrowing competes for limited savings and raises interest rates.

card.t: P1-13 · Policies of Telangana State · RARE and Kodangal Industrial Hub
card.hook: RARE = Rural Agriculture Region Economy; Kodangal = industrial hub focus.
card.scene: Think rural region → agriculture-linked economy → industries and jobs beyond Hyderabad. The November 2026 release highlights Kodangal as an industrial hub.
card.trap: Do not expand RARE as a road, renewable-energy or reservoir programme. Keep the official expansion and the Kodangal industrial-hub objective together.
card.q: What does RARE stand for in the Telangana Government's November 2026 release?
card.a: Rural Agriculture Region Economy.

card.t: P2-01 · Probability and Statistics · Point probability for a continuous random variable
card.hook: PDF height is density, not point probability; area over an interval gives probability.
card.scene: A single point has zero width under the density curve, so its area is zero. A non-zero interval has area and can have positive probability.
card.trap: f(a) can be positive even though P(X = a) = 0. Never read a density value as the probability at that exact point.
card.q: If X is continuous and f(2) = 0.4, what is P(X = 2)?
card.a: Zero. Probability is the integral of the density over an interval; a single point has zero area.

card.t: P2-02 · Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra · Counting binary relations
card.hook: A binary relation on n elements is any subset of A × A: n² ordered pairs give 2^(n²) relations.
card.scene: For each ordered pair, make one yes/no choice: include it in the relation or leave it out. With three elements there are nine ordered pairs and 2⁹ choices.
card.trap: Ordered pairs matter: (a,b) and (b,a) are different, and diagonal pairs (a,a) are included among the choices.
card.q: How many binary relations exist on a three-element set?

card.t: P2-03 · Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic · Ordinary generating functions
card.hook: For aₙ = n: A(x) = x/(1 − x)². For aₙ = 1: A(x) = 1/(1 − x).
card.scene: Start with the geometric series 1 + x + x² + … = 1/(1 − x). Differentiate and multiply by x to turn the coefficients into 0, 1, 2, 3, …
card.trap: Do not confuse the constant sequence 1,1,1,… with the counting sequence 0,1,2,3,…; their generating functions differ.
card.q: What is the ordinary generating function for aₙ = n, n ≥ 0?

card.t: P2-10 · Operating Systems · Paging and internal fragmentation
card.hook: Paging removes external fragmentation but can waste space inside the final page.
card.scene: A 10 KiB process needs three 4 KiB pages, giving 12 KiB allocated. The unused 2 KiB in the last page is internal fragmentation.
card.trap: Internal fragmentation is unused space inside an allocated block. External fragmentation is scattered free space between allocated blocks.
card.q: With 4 KiB pages, how much is wasted when a 10 KiB process gets three pages?
card.a: 2 KiB inside the last page: internal fragmentation.

card.t: P1-01 · Current affairs – Regional, National and International · ITIs to Advanced Technology Centres
card.hook: ITI → ATC: Telangana highlighted ITI upgrades into Advanced Technology Centres for skills and innovation (11 Nov 2026).
card.scene: Think of the progression as vocational training → advanced hands-on skills → innovation and employability.
card.trap: Do not confuse the ITI upgrade with the separate Skills University; the State Portal specifically names Advanced Technology Centres for ITIs.
card.q: What did the Telangana Government say ITIs had been upgraded into?
card.a: Advanced Technology Centres (ATCs).

card.t: P1-03 · General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology · Zener diode regulation
card.hook: Zener = reverse-biased breakdown → nearly fixed voltage VZ.
card.scene: The series resistor limits current; the Zener shunts extra current so the load voltage stays near VZ.
card.trap: An ordinary diode's reverse breakdown may damage it; Zener operation must remain within specified current and power limits.
card.q: How does a reverse-biased Zener diode regulate voltage?
card.a: It conducts in its designed breakdown region and holds its terminal voltage approximately at VZ.

card.t: P2-07 · Algorithms · Stack MULTIPOP amortized analysis
card.hook: Each pushed item is popped at most once → O(n) total work and O(1) amortized work per operation.
card.scene: One MULTIPOP can be long, but the same item cannot be removed twice; charge its removal to its earlier push.
card.trap: The worst-case cost of one operation is not the amortized cost over the full sequence.
card.q: Why is MULTIPOP amortized O(1) per operation?
card.a: Across n operations, each item is pushed once and popped at most once, so total work is O(n).

card.t: P2-11 · Databases · Safe tuple relational calculus
card.hook: Safe TRC = finite, domain-bounded results; output values must come from the formula's active domain.
card.scene: A query cannot return every imaginable tuple outside the data; tie result values to relation values or constants referenced by the formula.
card.trap: A syntactically valid TRC expression can still be unsafe; safety prevents infinite or domain-dependent results.
card.q: Why must a tuple relational calculus expression be safe?
card.a: To ensure its result is finite and all result values are drawn from the formula's domain.

card.t: P2-13 · Computer Networks · Digital signatures
card.hook: Private key signs; matching public key verifies; a signature does not provide confidentiality.
card.scene: The sender signs data with a private key; a recipient uses the corresponding public key to check the signature.
card.trap: Signing is not encrypting the document; confidentiality needs a separate encryption mechanism.
card.q: Which security property does a digital signature not provide by itself?
card.a: Confidentiality.

card.t: P1-02 · International Relations and Events · ICC complementarity
card.hook: Domestic courts first; the ICC is complementary, not a global appeal court.
card.scene: Picture two layers: national courts handle cases first; the ICC is a backstop when the State with jurisdiction is unwilling or unable genuinely to act.
card.trap: A domestic acquittal after genuine proceedings does not automatically send a case to the ICC. Article 17 tests admissibility and genuineness.
card.q: When may the ICC proceed under the principle of complementarity?
card.a: When the State with jurisdiction is unwilling or unable genuinely to investigate or prosecute, subject to the Rome Statute's other admissibility requirements.

card.t: P1-06 · Physical, Social and Economic Geography of India · Northeast monsoon
card.hook: Northeast monsoon = October–December; Tamil Nadu's southeast coast is a key beneficiary.
card.scene: After the southwest monsoon withdraws, the seasonal northeast flow and moisture from the Bay of Bengal bring important rain to the southeast coast.
card.trap: Do not say the northeast monsoon dominates rainfall across all India; most regions depend mainly on the southwest monsoon.
card.q: Which state is especially associated with northeast-monsoon rainfall?
card.a: Tamil Nadu, along with nearby southeast-peninsular subdivisions such as Puducherry and Karaikal.

card.t: P1-08 · Modern Indian History · Khilafat and the Ali Brothers
card.hook: Ali Brothers = Muhammad Ali + Shaukat Ali.
card.scene: Connect the post-First World War Ottoman Khalifa issue to the Ali brothers and Gandhi's joint Non-Cooperation–Khilafat mobilisation.
card.trap: Do not confuse the Ali brothers with other nationalist leaders or treat the Khilafat issue as a constitutional reform.
card.q: Who were popularly called the Ali Brothers?
card.a: Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.

card.t: P1-11 · Social Exclusion and Rights · Article 30(1)
card.hook: Article 29 = conserve language and culture; Article 30 = establish and administer minority educational institutions.
card.scene: Think of two doors: Article 29 protects cultural identity; Article 30 protects minority-run educational institutions.
card.trap: Article 30 covers religious and linguistic minorities. Article 29(1) concerns any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture.
card.q: What right is guaranteed by Article 30(1)?
card.a: Religious and linguistic minorities may establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

card.t: P2-06 · Programming in C · volatile versus atomic
card.hook: C volatile = observable accesses; it is not atomic and is not a thread lock.
card.scene: Think of volatile as a note to the compiler to respect certain accesses, not a traffic signal that safely coordinates two threads.
card.trap: Do not transfer Java volatile semantics to C. C thread synchronisation needs atomic operations or locks.
card.q: Does `volatile int` make a shared increment thread-safe?
card.a: No. It does not guarantee atomicity or inter-thread synchronisation; use a C atomic object or a mutex.

card.t: P2-09 · Compiler Design · loop unrolling
card.hook: Loop unrolling = copy the loop body to reduce loop-control overhead.
card.scene: Instead of doing one lap at a time, perform four repeated actions in one lap and advance the loop counter by four.
card.trap: Unrolling can increase code size and is safe only when the transformed loop preserves program behaviour. It is not loop-invariant code motion.
card.q: What compiler optimisation duplicates loop-body statements?
card.a: Loop unrolling.

card.t: P2-12 · Information Systems and Software Engineering · UML lifelines
card.hook: Sequence diagram: lifeline = participant; vertical direction = time; arrow = message.
card.scene: Imagine each participant as a vertical column. Message arrows pass between columns as the interaction progresses downward.
card.trap: A lifeline is not a class-inheritance line or a deployment node.
card.q: What does a lifeline represent in a UML sequence diagram?
card.a: A participant in the interaction and its presence over the course of the interaction.

card.t: P2-13 · Computer Networks · Stop-and-Wait ARQ utilisation
card.hook: Stop-and-Wait utilisation = 1/(1+2a), where a = propagation time ÷ frame transmission time.
card.scene: One frame travels out and its acknowledgement travels back; the sender waits through two propagation trips before sending the next frame.
card.trap: Do not use 1/(1+a). The ideal cycle includes two one-way propagation delays. Ignore ACK transmission and processing only when the question says so.
card.q: If a = 4, what is ideal Stop-and-Wait utilisation?

card.t: P2-14 · Web Technologies · servlet forward versus redirect
card.hook: forward = server-side handoff with the current request; redirect = 302 response and a new browser request.
card.scene: Forward is passing a file to another desk inside the same office. Redirect is sending the visitor to a new address.
card.trap: A forward must occur before the response is committed. sendRedirect commits a redirect response to the client.
card.q: Which servlet API performs an internal server-side handoff?
card.a: RequestDispatcher.forward(request, response).

card.t: P2-16 · Data Mining · SVM kernel trick
card.hook: Kernel trick = compute an inner product in an implicit feature space without building the mapped vectors.
card.scene: The kernel is a shortcut calculator: it returns the similarity as if the data had been lifted into a richer feature space.
card.trap: A kernel does not guarantee perfect separation. Kernel choice and regularisation still matter.
card.q: What does a kernel function provide in an SVM?
card.a: An inner product in the feature space, computed directly from the original input vectors.

card.t: P1-03 · General Science · First law of thermodynamics
card.hook: Heat in adds; work out subtracts: ΔU = Q − W.
card.scene: A piston absorbs 500 J and sends 200 J out as work; 300 J remains as extra internal energy.
card.trap: Here W means work done BY the gas. Work done ON the gas has the opposite sign in this convention.
card.q: A gas absorbs 120 J and does 45 J of work. What is ΔU?

card.t: P1-04 · Environment · Kigali Amendment and HFCs
card.hook: Kigali = HFC phase-down; Montreal originally targeted ozone-depleting substances.
card.scene: Picture two controls: Montreal reduces ODS; Kigali adds a gradual reduction of high-warming HFCs.
card.trap: HFCs generally do not deplete ozone, but they can have high global-warming potential.
card.q: Which chemical group is phased down under Kigali?
card.a: Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).

card.t: P1-07 · Telangana Geography · Dry deciduous forests
card.hook: Telangana's broad forest memory: largely dry deciduous, with teak and dry-forest associates.
card.scene: Imagine teak beside Terminalia and Pterocarpus; many trees shed leaves in the dry season.
card.trap: Do not confuse the State's broad natural vegetation with evergreen, mangrove or alpine forests.
card.q: Which broad forest type does the Telangana Forest Department describe as prevalent?
card.a: Dry deciduous.

card.t: P1-12 · Telangana Culture · Lambadi dance
card.hook: Lambadi is listed among Narayanpet's popular dance forms.
card.scene: Picture a colourful group performance and connect Lambadi with Telangana's Lambadi/Banjara cultural heritage.
card.trap: Do not swap it with Perini Sivatandavam (warrior dance), Cheriyal scroll painting or Pembarthi brassware.
card.q: Which dance form appears in Telangana Tourism's Narayanpet profile?
card.a: Lambadi.

card.t: P2-04 · Digital Logic · JK race-around
card.hook: J = K = 1 + a long level-high clock → repeated toggles.
card.scene: The JK output keeps flipping while the clock gate stays open; a master-slave pair provides a controlled hand-off.
card.trap: A single toggle is the truth-table action. Race-around means repeated toggles within one active pulse.
card.q: Name two common ways to prevent race-around.
card.a: Use a master-slave JK flip-flop or an edge-triggered flip-flop.

card.t: P2-05 · COA · Daisy-chain bus arbitration
card.hook: The grant travels down the chain; the first requester captures it.
card.scene: Imagine a baton passed from the arbiter through devices; the first waiting device stops it.
card.trap: Priority is fixed by physical position. A low-priority device can starve if nearer devices keep requesting.
card.q: Which requester wins when several request together?
card.a: The requesting device nearest to the arbiter in the chain.

card.t: P2-11 · DBMS · View serializability
card.hook: View equivalence = same initial reads, same read-from source, same final writer.
card.scene: Remember three checkpoints: where a read starts, whose write it reads, and who writes last.
card.trap: Conflict-serializable implies view-serializable; blind writes can make the reverse false.
card.q: Why can a view-serializable schedule still have a cyclic conflict graph?
card.a: Blind writes can create conflicting order edges without changing read-from or final-write equivalence.

card.t: P2-13 · Networks · Binary exponential backoff
card.hook: After collision i, choose K from 0 through 2^min(i,10) − 1 slots.
card.scene: The window doubles: collision 1 gives 0–1, collision 2 gives 0–3, collision 3 gives 0–7.
card.trap: Count the collision that just occurred; after the third collision the range is 0–7, not 0–3.
card.q: What range is available after collision three?
card.a: 0 through 7 slot times.

card.t: P2-14 · Web Technologies · XML Schema facets
card.hook: XSD = XML structure + rich datatypes + value facets.
card.scene: A schema can say age is an integer and bound it; DTD mainly describes structure with limited typing.
card.trap: xs:sequence orders child elements; minInclusive/maxInclusive constrain numeric values.
card.q: Which facets set inclusive numeric bounds?
card.a: xs:minInclusive and xs:maxInclusive.

card.t: P2-15 · Java · Initialization order
card.hook: Static: Parent → Child. Instance: Parent initializers → Parent constructor → Child initializers → Child constructor.
card.scene: Build the inheritance tree from top down; the parent finishes its instance setup before the child.
card.trap: Child instance blocks do not run before the parent constructor.
card.q: What runs immediately before the Child constructor body?
card.a: Child instance field initializers and instance initializer blocks.

card.t: P1-01 · Current affairs – Regional, National and International · IYRP 2026: FAO leads
card.hook: 2026 = Rangelands + Pastoralists; FAO leads.
card.scene: Rangeland ecosystems support pastoral livelihoods; the UN observance links land stewardship, mobility and sustainable investment.
card.trap: Do not confuse FAO's lead-agency role with UNEP's wider environmental mandate or IFAD's rural-development financing.
card.q: Which UN agency leads the 2026 International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists?
card.a: FAO, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. The UN General Assembly declared 2026 the IYRP.

card.t: P1-03 · General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology · Aditya-L1 at Sun–Earth L1
card.hook: L1 = Long, uninterrupted look at the Sun.
card.scene: Sun — Sun–Earth L1 (Aditya-L1 halo orbit) — Earth; schematic, not to scale.
card.trap: L1 is not a point of zero gravity, and Aditya-L1 is not in Earth orbit or lunar orbit.
card.q: What is the main observation advantage of the L1 halo orbit?
card.a: A near-continuous view of the Sun without Earth occultation or eclipses; ISRO places L1 about 1.5 million km from Earth.

card.t: P1-04 · Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies · IMD heat-wave thresholds
card.hook: Plains: 40°C base; 4.5 / 6.5 departure; 45 / 47 actual.
card.scene: Two separate routes: departure from normal (4.5–6.4°C = heat wave; ≥6.5°C = severe) or actual maximum (≥45°C = heat wave; ≥47°C = severe).
card.trap: Do not mix departure-based thresholds with absolute-maximum thresholds, and do not omit the plains station base condition.
card.q: For plains, what departure threshold marks a severe heat wave?
card.a: At least 6.5°C above normal, with the station maximum temperature at least 40°C; actual-temperature criteria are a separate route.

card.t: P1-11 · Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies · 103rd Amendment: EWS
card.hook: 103rd = 15(6) education + 16(6) employment.
card.scene: 103rd Amendment → Article 15(6) (education) and Article 16(6) (public employment); up to 10%.
card.trap: Do not confuse EWS clauses (6) with older clauses (4), and do not treat EWS as another name for SC/ST/OBC reservations.
card.q: Which clauses enable EWS special provisions and reservation?
card.a: Articles 15(6) and 16(6). The 103rd Amendment added these provisions, enabling up to 10% EWS reservation.

card.t: P2-04 · Digital Logic · Asynchronous versus synchronous reset
card.hook: ASYNC = acts without a clock; SYNC = waits for an edge.
card.scene: Compare a reset asserted between clock edges: asynchronous reset changes Q immediately; synchronous reset is sampled at the active edge.
card.trap: Do not call a reset a clock pulse. Asynchronous assertion is immediate, but de-assertion near a clock edge needs care.
card.q: If the clock is stopped, which reset can still force a flip-flop into its reset state?
card.a: An asynchronous reset. It acts independently of the clock; safe designs commonly synchronize its de-assertion.

card.t: P2-06 · Programming and Data Structures · C signed versus unsigned overflow
card.hook: Signed int overflow = undefined; unsigned = modulo wrap.
card.scene: Signed int: out-of-range result → undefined behavior. Unsigned int: result reduced modulo one more than its maximum value.
card.trap: Two's-complement hardware does not make signed overflow wraparound defined by standard C.
card.q: Which integer type has defined modulo arithmetic on overflow in C?
card.a: Unsigned integer types. For ordinary signed int, an out-of-range arithmetic result has undefined behavior.

card.t: P2-12 · Information Systems and Software Engineering · UML aggregation versus composition
card.hook: Hollow diamond = shared; filled diamond = composite.
card.scene: Whole ◇—Part (shared) versus Whole ◆—Part (composite); a composite part belongs to at most one whole at a time.
card.trap: Do not claim shared aggregation has the same strict lifecycle rule; UML leaves its precise semantics to the application/modeler.
card.q: What happens to a contained part when its composite whole is deleted?
card.a: Under composite aggregation, the part object is deleted with the whole unless it was removed beforehand.

card.t: P2-15 · OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA · Java wait() and monitor ownership
card.hook: wait releases; notify wakes; waiter must reacquire.
card.scene: T1 holds monitor → wait releases it and enters the wait set → T2 notifies while holding it → T1 wakes and later reacquires.
card.trap: notify() does not hand over the lock immediately; wait() requires monitor ownership, and condition checks belong in a while loop.
card.q: Which monitor does obj.wait() release?
card.a: Only the monitor for obj; the waiting thread must reacquire it before wait() returns.

card.t: P2-16 · Data Mining · Closed versus maximal frequent itemsets
card.hook: Closed: no same-support superset. Maximal: no frequent superset.
card.scene: Closed itemsets preserve support information; maximal itemsets are a smaller boundary summary but lose support details for subsets.
card.trap: A closed itemset may still have a frequent superset with lower support; then it is closed but not maximal.
card.q: What distinguishes a closed itemset from a maximal frequent itemset?
card.a: Closed means no proper superset has the same support. Maximal means no proper superset is frequent.
